title: Definitive intake playbook for unversioned open weights
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Purpose: Clarify required metadata, acceptance criteria, and operational controls for intake of open-source model weights that do not ship explicit semantic version tags. This playbook defines the 'unversioned intake' pathway, when to require a soft pin vs. hard pin, compatibility signal checks at ingestion, and rollback/fallback requirements for runtime-safety. The goal is to reduce manual triage time and avoid serving surprises from unversioned community variants while preserving fast admission for experimental weights.
acceptance_criteria: Intake schema: every open-weight submission must include tokenizer checksum, model architecture tag, anchor seed commit (git/uri) or origin build identifier, and preferred inference config. Automated validator returns pass/warn/fail with clear remediation messaging.

Compatibility checks: automated vector of compatibility signals is executed and persisted (tokenizer mapping, vocab size delta, kv-cache format, dtype/quantization expected, and expected max-seq). Tickets must capture at least 3 failing signals to reject admission.

Pinning policy: define and document when to auto-apply 'soft-pin' (catalog metadata only) vs. require 'hard-pin' (runtime pinned variant). Soft-pin must generate a 30-day review reminder and an automated test run; hard-pin requires PM+Eng approval and rollout plan.

Runtime smoke: every accepted unversioned weight must pass a 3-sample smoke suite (generation coherence, basic safety filters, and latency baseline within 2x of the catalog median for similar-arch models). Failure opens intake review task for eng triage.

Fallback mapping: catalog entry contains a fallback variant (pinned or smaller model) and a routing policy so the request path can switch automatically if latency or error SLOs degrade beyond thresholds.
Telemetry and alerts: onboarding should wire up eval-set regressions and QoE monitors. A regression alert template and alert owner must be assigned before shipping to production routes.
Docs & UX: acceptance requires a concise PRD + intake checklist in Confluence and an intake form update in the Console to capture required fields and signed-ack for unversioned acceptance.
Security/compliance: attestation field for license and export-control must be present; if any license is incompatible, intake must be rejected automatically.
Ops playbook: roll-forward and rollback steps documented with links to dashboards and runbooks for on-call and SRE teams.
decisions: Adopt a triage-first flow: automated validator gate + human review for any 'warn' results.
Soft-pin semantics: soft-pin = catalog-level pointer that can be automatically remapped by the runtime; it does not require immediate runtime pinning but creates periodic review alarms.
Hard-pin semantics: hard-pin = runtime-pinned image/weights enforced by serving runtime and requires explicit release and rollback hooks.
Compatibility vector chosen (initial): tokenizer_checksum, tokenizer_mapping_score, vocab_delta, kv_cache_hash, dtype_hint, max_seq_hint, warmup_token_profile.
Require fallback variant on intake for any unversioned weight destined for hosted routes.
scope_changes: Initial PRD asked to require explicit semver for all models; changed to allow 'unversioned' pathway with stricter validator and monitoring after Eng/PM tradeoff discussion on 2026-02-27.
Removed requirement for full benchmark suite pre-admission (too slow) and replaced with a 3-sample smoke run and staged post-admit profiler pass during the first 24h of traffic.
Added security attestation after Legal signaled license ambiguity in community weights (2026-03-03).
rollout_plan: Week 0 (feature freeze): merge validator + intake form changes behind feature flag; update Confluence PRD (owner: Ravi).
Week 1: run a pilot intake with 5 community submissions (internal-only catalog) and capture validator outputs; iterate on messaging.
Week 2: enable soft-pin pathway for 'sandboxed' hosted routes with telemetry enabled; require fallback variant mapping.
Week 3: open intake to broader internal teams and require PM+Eng signoff for any hard-pinned runtime exposures.
Post-rollout (30 days): evaluate false-positive/negative rates for validator signals and adjust thresholds; document lessons and convert to hard SLO targets.
Rollback trigger: >2.5x error-rate increase or >30% QoE regression on a pinned route within 6 hours triggers automated rollback to fallback variant and a postmortem.
